intent: Switch between panels that share the same screen space, showing exactly one at a time.
typical_uses: Grouping related views that do not need to be compared side by side
Switching between differently-shaped content behind a shared header, where only one need be visible or interactive at once

dont_use_when.situation: Sequential, gated steps that need validation before the user may move to the next one

instead.note: This kit ships no stepper component. Tabs imply free jumping between every panel; a gated wizard must prevent that, which nothing here does.

dont_use_when.situation: Content the user needs to compare at a glance

instead.target: a layout that keeps every section visible at once (a row or grid of Card, for instance)
instead.note: Tabs hide every panel but the active one, so nothing behind the active tab is ever visible beside it.

dont_use_when.situation: Picking a mode or option with no panel to show per choice
Sections that may be open at the same time

invariants.text: `value` and `defaultValue` are both accepted; `defaultValue` seeds the initial state and is ignored afterwards, and when `value` is given it wins and the component follows it on every render.

With `orientation` at its default of `horizontal`, every part - the root, the list, each trigger and the open panel - stamps a matching `data-orientation` attribute that lays the list above its panel and moves focus between triggers with the left/right arrow keys; switching to `vertical` puts the list beside its panel and moves focus with up/down instead. No other prop needs to change to switch it.

anti_patterns.dont: Give two TabsTrigger/TabsContent pairs the same value
anti_patterns.do_instead: Give every pair a unique value - Base UI matches a panel to its tab by exact value equality, and a duplicate leaves one panel unreachable

anti_patterns.dont: Omit defaultValue/value while leaving the first TabsTrigger disabled
anti_patterns.do_instead: Set defaultValue (or value) explicitly to an enabled tab's value - Base UI falls back to the next enabled tab client-side, but it cannot do that during server-side rendering, so the server- and client-rendered output would disagree

a11y.by: Base UI's Tabs.Root - tablist/tab/tabpanel role wiring and keyboard navigation between triggers - exercised by tabs.test.tsx's "stamps data-orientation on every part, defaulting to horizontal" and "switches every part to vertical orientation and keeps arrow-key navigation on its own axis" assertions

value.states: value is an opaque identifier, typed any by Base UI, compared by identity against a TabsTrigger's own value
value.because: Base UI's TabsRootProps types `value` as `TabsTab.Value | undefined`, where `TabsTab.Value` is `any | null` - not interpreted, only compared by identity, so no JSON Schema type can state what it holds beyond "present or null". tabs.md's example uses string values (`defaultValue="account"`), which is what a reader should reach for.

defaultValue.states: defaultValue is the same opaque any-typed identifier as value, seeding the initial selection
defaultValue.because: Same `TabsTab.Value` type as `value` above, unchecked in the same half - the uncontrolled starting selection is compared by identity against each trigger's own `value`, and no schema can state what a caller's own identifier looks like.

onValueChange.states: onValueChange is a callback, not a value
onValueChange.because: `(value: TabsTab.Value, eventDetails) => void` - a function of the opaque value type plus Base UI's own event-details object. No JSON Schema type covers a function.

render.states: render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies
render.because: Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the root's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - neither expressible in JSON Schema.

style.states: style accepts a function of the root's state as well as a plain style object
style.because: Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)` so a caller can style off the primitive's own state (orientation, tabActivationDirection). A JSON Schema `object` would reject the function form, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through tabs.module.css, not through this.

bad.title: Two panels sharing the same value
bad.code:
<Tabs defaultValue="account">
  <TabsList>
    <TabsTrigger value="account">Account</TabsTrigger>
    <TabsTrigger value="account">Duplicate</TabsTrigger>
  </TabsList>
  <TabsContent value="account">One panel, two triggers pointing at it.</TabsContent>
</Tabs>
bad.why: Base UI matches a panel to its tab by exact value equality; a duplicate value leaves the second trigger with no panel of its own to activate.
